open_questions: Inter-sector depth scatter (80% change, chi2 21.53 dof 3) – likely unocculted spots on active Teff 3145 K M-dwarf with RUWE 1.204, RUWE 1.204 excess_noise_sig 6.447, or spot-crossings, needs follow-up transit chromatic depth and radial velocities to confirm achromatic and rule out variability; durations ratio 1.464 with star_density_penalty 87.63 suggests longer than central for this low-mass star.
dossier.public_summary: A 2.3 Earth-radius flat-bottomed dip repeats every 14.1 days on an M-dwarf 35 parsecs away. There is no odd/even difference, no secondary eclipse and no nearby star able to mimic the signal, so a planet is the best explanation despite a strong change in depth between sectors that matches spot activity on the small star.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed (not V-shaped) transit, favours planet over grazing EB/star eclipse.
Odd and even depths identical (8614 vs 8747 ppm), no evidence for binary at twice period 28.2 d.
No credible secondary eclipse (snr below 5 and only 3.699, best_brightening_snr 2.334), secondary_phase_offset 0.2685 not near 0.5.
No star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can cause the 8746 ppm dip even with 25% eclipse; closest that could at 37.4 arcsec would need 0.2647 depth, so blend ruled out by density.
Undiluted depth 8820 ppm on 0.2261 Rsun M-dwarf implies 2.316 Rearth planet size, well below stellar regime.

Depth varies 80.83% (8747, 5861, 6500, 11861 ppm) with p_constant 0.00008159 and transit_depths p_consistent 1.4850171536779071e-05, but transit_depths outliers [] and shape flat argue variability not a few spurious events; sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source is real scatter, not grounds to reject alone.

Centroid inconclusive (no sector with clear difference image) cannot place dip off-target, and centroid_all did not run, so on-target assumed; inconclusive is not positive evidence for neighbourhood blend given 0 plausible neighbours.
